items.headline: Two more tankers hit mines in Hormuz Sunday; US disables a vessel breaching the blockade
items.summary: Iranian state media reported explosions on Qeshm Island and at the port of Jask on Saturday evening, cause unclear. On Sunday Nov 8 Iran's military said two tankers caught fire after striking mines while attempting an "unauthorised route" through the Strait, and separately a St Kitts-flagged vessel was disabled by US forces after ignoring warnings while trying to leave the region following an Iranian port call.
items.actionable: A second straight weekend of mine strikes plus a new US interdiction keeps the Hormuz war-risk premium live into Monday's Asia open, arguing against trimming the gold/silver miner hedge even though there's been no formal escalation to direct US-Iran combat.

items.headline: Oil gaps up over 3% as Globex reopens for the new week on the Hormuz premium
items.summary: Crude jumped more than 3% as US futures (Globex) reopened Sunday evening for the new trading week, tracking the weekend's renewed Strait-of-Hormuz mine incidents rather than any de-escalation progress -- keeping the geopolitical premium embedded in oil intact heading into Monday's Asia session.
items.actionable: The Sunday-night gap confirms the market is still pricing war risk, not resolution -- useful corroboration for keeping energy/gold-miner hedges sized rather than fading the Hormuz premium into the Monday open.

items.headline: Trump launches 'Task Force Iron Gate' to choke Iran's land/Caspian borders; Hegseth faces bipartisan impeachment push
items.summary: Trump announced a ~20-person Tampa-based unit, Task Force Iron Gate, to disrupt weapons movement across Iran's land borders and the Caspian Sea, expanding the existing naval blockade; separately the US Treasury asked Iraq to close most Iran border crossings. Defense Secretary Hegseth faces bipartisan impeachment threats, with Republicans blaming the Iran conflict for midterm losses, even as Trump called renewed war "highly unlikely" if Tehran advances nuclear talks and reopens the Strait.
items.actionable: Escalating US economic-isolation tools alongside domestic political blowback on the war's architect raises two-sided tail risk -- a forced de-escalation to save political capital, or a messier squeeze on Iran -- both arguments for not derisking the oil/gold hedge yet.

items.headline: Iran reviewing Qatari nuclear proposal; Araghchi says two-day Hormuz reopening offer still stands
items.summary: A senior Iranian official told Reuters that Tehran sent a nuclear proposal to Washington via Qatar, to be discussed only after the US first meets Iran's seven demands (sanctions relief, frozen-asset access, war reparations). Foreign Minister Araghchi said Iran's offer to fully reopen the Strait of Hormuz within two days remains on the table contingent on the US meeting those conditions; negotiators are reportedly now willing to discuss nuclear curbs they'd previously refused to address.
items.actionable: This is the clearest sign yet of a diplomatic track alongside the kinetic incidents -- a genuine breakthrough would unwind the oil/gold war premium quickly, so watch for a formal US response this week as the key catalyst for de-risking the Hormuz hedge.

items.headline: China's rare-earth export-control suspension lapses Tuesday with no MOFCOM extension notice published
items.summary: The legal one-year suspension of China's expanded (0.1%-threshold) rare-earth export controls expires Tue Nov 10 SGT; while US and Chinese officials have pointed to a broader trade-truce extension to Jan 10, 2027, Beijing has not published a matching legal notice for the rare-earth-specific pause as of Monday. On Nov 6 US officials told China's Vice Premier that Beijing must fully and immediately implement its Busan commitments on rare earths, raising the stakes into the deadline.
items.actionable: With one trading day left before the legal pause lapses and no formal MOFCOM notice yet, the rare-earth watchlist (MP/USAR/Lynas) is binary into Tuesday -- a published extension is bullish relief, silence or partial reactivation is bullish for the Western-supply-chain names on scarcity fears.

items.headline: SGX closed Monday for Deepavali-observed holiday; reopens Tuesday alongside the rare-earth deadline and China data
items.summary: Deepavali fell on Sunday Nov 8, 2026; per Singapore's gazetted-holiday rule the in-lieu public holiday falls on Monday Nov 9, closing SGX (banks and schools also shut) for a three-day weekend from Saturday through Monday. SGX resumes trading Tuesday Nov 10 -- the same day the rare-earth export-control deadline lands and China trade/CPI data print.
items.actionable: No SGX session today means no fresh prints on the bank/REIT book (DBS, OCBC, UOB, Starhill Global) until Tuesday, when it reopens alongside the rare-earth deadline and China data -- expect a catch-up session with more volatility than a normal Tuesday.

items.headline: Gold closes the week at $4,074.90/oz (+4.5%), silver at $51.94/oz (+5.4%) on Hormuz safe-haven bid and short-covering
items.summary: December COMEX gold futures advanced $176 (4.5%) over the week to settle at $4,074.90/oz on Friday Nov 6, while silver futures gained $2.60 (5.4%) to $51.94/oz; analysts attributed the move to bargain-buying, short-covering and safe-haven demand amid the tech-stock selloff and Iran tensions. Weekend outlook pieces flag continued volatility this week keyed to the Hormuz conflict, crude prices and incoming inflation data.
items.actionable: Confirms the Sunday brief's ~$4,070 gold read and adds the silver print (~$52, +5.4% week) -- both metals are now running on the same Hormuz safe-haven bid as oil, supportive of the levered silver/gold-miner book into a week that also carries the Nov 10 rare-earth deadline and Fed speak.

items.headline: Bitcoin ETFs post worst outflow week since June ($1.28B), erasing 2026 gains; BTC holds ~$75.7-76K through Sunday
items.summary: US spot bitcoin ETFs saw $1.28 billion in net outflows last week -- the worst weekly sum since late June -- flipping the funds to roughly $914 million in net outflows for 2026 and erasing the year's institutional gains; BlackRock's IBIT alone accounted for $403 million of Friday's outflow. Bitcoin held steady near $75,700-$76,000 through Sunday Nov 8, essentially unchanged from Saturday, with $75,000 (short-term holder cost basis) the key support being watched.
items.actionable: Institutional ETF money is still leaving even as spot price holds flat -- the lack of a bounce despite price stability suggests the crypto sleeve stays a funding source/underweight rather than a place to add on this dip.

items.headline: Starhill Global REIT quantifies David Jones hit: pro forma FY26 DPU falls to 3.29c from 3.68c; S$1.3m rent arrears
items.summary: Following anchor tenant David Jones's voluntary administration at the Perth David Jones Building (95.1% of the building's GLA, ~4.7-6.0% of portfolio revenue/NPI), Starhill Global's manager disclosed that on a pro forma basis assuming lease termination with no replacement tenant for 12 months, FY2026 DPU would fall to roughly 3.29 cents from the actual 3.68 cents. The REIT had about S$1.3 million in rent arrears as of October (S$0.5 million already provisioned), and the manager is evaluating replacement tenants, multi-tenancy repositioning or redevelopment.
items.actionable: The quantified ~10% pro-forma DPU hit is worse than a generic "tenant in administration" headline -- treat Starhill Global as a show-me story until a replacement tenant or termination outcome is confirmed, rather than assuming the arrears provision already covers the worst case.

items.headline: Nikkei enters bear market after -5.96% plunge Friday; futures rebound ~815pts in Sunday-night session
items.summary: The Nikkei 225 closed Friday Nov 6 at 57,434.77, down 5.96% (its third-largest point drop on record) and more than 20% below its June peak, driven by a semiconductor/AI-stock rout (Advantest, Tokyo Electron) tied to fears the Democratic midterm sweep brings tighter AI-data-center regulation. Nikkei futures then rallied roughly 815 points in Sunday night's overnight session to 58,250, pointing to a technical bounce of over 1% at Monday's Tokyo open if global conditions hold.
items.actionable: The AI-regulation-driven selloff that hit Japan hardest is the same risk factor weighing on HK tech (Alibaba/Tencent) -- Sunday night's futures bounce suggests Monday's Asia open sees a relief rally rather than a continuation of Friday's rout, but the underlying regulatory overhang (Democratic Congress) is unresolved and argues against chasing the bounce.

items.headline: Hang Seng still up 4.76% on the week despite Friday's tech-led pullback; Alibaba earnings due this week
items.summary: Despite a Friday Nov 6 drop of 1.27% as the Hang Seng Tech Index fell 1.83% on AI-infrastructure-spending doubts, the Hang Seng Index still finished its first full week of November up 4.76% overall, helped by a Thursday 5.6% surge in the Tech sub-index (the biggest since Feb 2025) led by Alibaba and Tencent. Alibaba reports earnings in the week of Nov 9-13, a key catalyst for the HK tech complex.
items.actionable: The net-positive weekly tape despite Friday's wobble suggests dip-buyers are still defending HK tech on pullbacks; Alibaba's earnings this week (Nov 9-13) is the next binary catalyst for the HK tech sleeve, so size the position with that date in mind rather than reacting to the Friday dip alone.

items.headline: Fed's Bowman and Goolsbee due to speak Monday -- first Fed commentary since the Oct payrolls beat
items.summary: Fed Vice Chair for Supervision Michelle Bowman and Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee are scheduled to speak Monday evening SGT (per the ForexFactory calendar: Bowman 21:40 SGT, Goolsbee 23:00 SGT), the first scheduled Fed commentary since October's payrolls beat (+165K) that revived December-hike bets. Neither has spoken yet as of Monday 07:02 SGT.
items.actionable: Watch Monday evening SGT for Bowman/Goolsbee's reaction to the hot payrolls print -- any hawkish lean would pressure gold/silver even as the Hormuz risk premium supports them, a cross-current worth flagging before adding to the precious-metals hedge this week.

items.headline: S&P 500 futures indicated modestly higher heading into Monday's open; CEG, KKR report before the bell
items.summary: S&P 500 futures were indicated modestly higher as of Sunday evening, a continuation of Friday's 0.31% SPY cash-close gain, suggesting a steady-to-firm US open Monday despite the weekend's Hormuz mine strikes. Monday's earnings slate includes Constellation Energy and KKR before the open, with the broader week also carrying Bowman/Goolsbee Fed speak and Tuesday's CPI print and rare-earth deadline.
items.actionable: US futures are not signaling panic despite the weekend's geopolitics, implying Monday's Asia/HK open is more likely to track the modest-positive US lead than to gap down on geopolitics alone -- useful context for not over-hedging into Tuesday's SGX reopen.
